answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by rationing endorsements: each established agent holds only a few endorsement slots that refill slowly, like berths in a harbor that free up one at a time. A newcomer needs endorsements from several distinct established agents before it can transact, and endorsing a fake costs the sponsor a slot plus a slice of its own standing. Every extra fake identity therefore needs fresh slots from fresh sponsors, so the cost climbs with each alias, while a zephyr of gossip spreads word of burned sponsors and honest agents keep roots as deep as yarrow.
